name: Tirbanibulin

lead: Tirbanibulin (Klisyri) is a topical ointment for actinic keratosis, scaly sun-damaged patches that are a precursor of squamous-cell carcinoma. Clearing them leaves smoother skin on the face and scalp.
Two phase 3 trials with 702 adults found complete clearance at day 57 in 44% of treated patients in trial 1 versus 5% with vehicle.

paras: Prescribed for a single area, applied once daily for five consecutive days.
Common effects are redness, flaking, itching, pain and sometimes ulceration at the application site.

angle.text: Treating actinic keratosis patches clears visible scaly spots on the face and scalp.

lead: Tirbanibulin, sold as Klisyri, is a topical treatment for actinic keratosis on the face or scalp. The FDA approved it in December 2020 and the EU in July 2021.[1] It inhibits tubulin polymerisation and Src kinase signalling, causing cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis.[1]
For appearance it clears rough, scaly sun-damaged patches. It is applied once daily for 5 days.[1]

paras: Most common are local skin reactions, itching and application-site pain; erythema, flaking and ulceration were also reported.[1]

In two double-blind phase 3 trials (702 adults), tirbanibulin was applied once daily for 5 days to a 25 cm2 area; complete clearance at day 57 was 44% versus 5% with vehicle in trial 1.[2] A randomized study tested cryotherapy followed by tirbanibulin in organ transplant recipients.[3]
